label: Anatolian buffalo

links.name: Wikipedia: List of water buffalo breeds

names.text: The list page gives Anadolu Mandası as the Turkish name, and Camız, Camış, Kömüş and Dombay as regional names.

about.text: The Anatolian buffalo is a Turkish water buffalo kept for milk and draught, mainly in the Marmara and Black Sea regions and in southern Turkey. It is classed as a Mediterranean-type buffalo.

sources.text: The list page places the breed in 'the Marmara and Black Sea regions, and South Turkey'. No formation date is given.
Found in WebSearch text only, not opened: a FAO buffalo breeds chapter lists about 110,000 Anatolian buffaloes, from 1999-2004 data. The year given is the end of that range.

links.name: Avesis: A research on milk yield, milk composition and body weights of Anatolian buffaloes

sources.text: Bitlis province, 1,448 Anatolian buffaloes, Indian Journal of Animal Research 2017. The abstract gives least-squares means of 763.99 +/- 18.66 kg lactation milk yield and 262.63 +/- 8.37 days lactation length. A search snippet of the same paper shows 163.99 kg, which looks like a typo.

facts.v: Turkey's total water buffalo population is reported to have risen from about 84,000 to 142,000 over a decade, linked to a gene-resource protection programme. This is the national total, not the Anatolian breed alone.

gaps: No DAD-IS entry or risk status found. The only breed-level count (110,000) is a 1999-2004 figure from search text. No formation date. The yield and composition come from one province (Bitlis, 2017), and the same paper's 163.99 kg figure in a search snippet looks like a typo. Other Turkish studies gave different yields, but I did not open their pages, so they are not used.
